info.name: Init Server API
info.description:
Reusable starter API: admin, vendor, associate and customer portals.

Seeded users (npm run db:reset creates these, all with the same password):
- Admin: admin@test.com
- Vendor: vendor@test.com
- BA: ba@test.com
- Customer: customer@test.com

HOW TO RUN (QA)
1. Start from a fresh database: npm run db:reset -- <dbName> (drops the database in MONGO_URI and flushes REDIS_DB, then seeds; <dbName> must match the database MONGO_URI points at, or it refuses). Several requests create fixed accounts, so a second run without a reset fails on duplicates.
2. Set the {{password}} collection variable to the seed password (printed by the seed: Qa-Test-99 unless SEED_ADMIN_PASSWORD is set). Change {{serverUrl}} and {{baseUrl}} if the server is not on localhost:8000.
3. For a full run, raise the login rate limit (e.g. RATE_LIMIT_LOGIN_MAX=1000) or the run hits 429 - the collection logs in about 35 times from one IP. Keep RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED=true: "Auth Scenarios / Sessions, Providers and Limits / 1." checks the RateLimit headers. If you step through by hand, make SESSION_EXPIRY_MS longer than your pauses.
4. Run the folders top to bottom, in order. Each test script saves the ids later requests use ({{baReferralCode}}, {{customerUserId}}, {{roleId}}, {{sid}} ...); nothing has to be copied by hand.
5. The 20 requests named "[manual] ..." need a human: an emailed code ({{otp}}) or a real Google ID token ({{googleIdToken}}). Their descriptions say exactly what to paste. Skip them in an unattended run; no request depends on them unless it is also marked [manual].
6. Upload requests need a file picked in the "file" form field (any JPG, PNG or WEBP under 2 MB) - Postman cannot embed one in a collection.

FOLDER ORDER: Health, Routing, Associate, Vendor, Admin, Customer, Auth Scenarios, Role Scenarios. Order matters: Routing must run before any login (it checks requests that carry no session cookie); Associate creates the referral code Vendor uses (Register Vendor (With Referral) and Request Additional Role); Role Scenarios runs last and puts back every role setting it changes. Any path that leaves a role APPROVED - auto-approval at signup or on request-role, an admin approval, an admin creating a user - activates the PENDING referral for that role and creates a referral code for a BUSINESS_ASSOCIATE or VENDOR that has none. A role granted by self-service request-role is pushed into the caller's live sessions, so Switch Role right after Request Additional Role works without logging in again. Each portal folder ends with "Sessions, Sign-out and Recovery", which logs that account out.

ROLE SCENARIOS: Role Requests turns auto-approval off for VENDOR and BUSINESS_ASSOCIATE so three requests stay PENDING in any environment, then the admin approves two and rejects one - an approved role is switchable at once, without logging in again, and an approval activates the referral the request carried and gives a new associate its referral code. Role Toggle Live Sync deactivates VENDOR while its holder is logged in (that session is revoked, their other-portal session loses the role) and re-activates it. Admin Portal Login as SUPER_ADMIN briefly opens SUPER_ADMIN to self-registration to make an account that holds SUPER_ADMIN but not ADMIN, shows it can log in to the admin portal, then closes registration and suspends the account.

ADMIN ROLE REQUESTS: GET /admin/role-requests (status = PENDING (default), APPROVED, REJECTED, SUSPENDED or REVOKED; roleCode; page; limit), PATCH /admin/role-requests/:id/approve, PATCH /admin/role-requests/:id/reject (optional body {"reason": "..."}). Deciding a request that is no longer PENDING is 400 ROLE_REQUEST_NOT_PENDING; an unknown id is 404 ROLE_REQUEST_NOT_FOUND.

UNKNOWN ROUTES: JSON 404 {"code": "ROUTE_NOT_FOUND"}. A POST under a portal path that carries that portal's session cookie but no x-csrf-token is still 403 AUTH_CSRF_MISSING, because CSRF runs before routing.

URLs: {{baseUrl}} includes /api/v1. {{serverUrl}} is the bare server, used only by /health and one Routing request.

Auth: an opaque session in a per-portal httpOnly cookie, stored in Redis, one per device. Postman's cookie jar sends it automatically. There is no Bearer token.

CSRF: login and OAuth responses include data.csrfToken. A collection-level test script stores it as {{adminCsrf}}, {{vendorCsrf}}, {{associateCsrf}} or {{customerCsrf}} by the portal in the URL. Every non-GET request that needs a session sends it as the x-csrf-token header; without it the server returns 403.

PASSWORD POLICY: PASSWORD_MIN_LENGTH characters (default 8) and not a known-breached password (HIBP).

item.name: Routing
item.description: Unknown routes answer JSON 404 ROUTE_NOT_FOUND. These run before any login so no session cookie is sent: verifyCsrf skips a request with no session, so an unknown POST is a 404, not a 403. If your Postman cookie jar still holds a session for this host from an earlier run, clear it first.

item.name: Unknown route (POST, no session) - expect 404 not 403
item.description: No session cookie and no x-csrf-token. CSRF only guards requests that carry a session, so this reaches the 404 handler.

exec: pm.test('404 Not Found - CSRF skipped without a session', () => pm.response.to.have.status(404));

item.name: Associate
item.description: Runs first: Get My Referral Code saves {{baReferralCode}}, which the Vendor folder needs.

item.name: Request Additional Role
item.description: The development seed auto-approves VENDOR, so this is granted at once and the account also gets a referral code (Get My Referral Code below relies on that). In production the request stays PENDING until an admin approves it (see Role Scenarios / Role Requests).

item.name: Switch Role

exec: pm.test('200 OK - switched WITHOUT logging in again', () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));

item.description: No login since Request Additional Role: a role granted by self-service auto-approval is pushed into the caller's live sessions (sessionService.syncRoles), so the session that asked for VENDOR can switch to it at once. switch-role checks the roles held by the session, not the database.

item.name: Get My Referral Code
item.description: Saves {{baReferralCode}}; the Vendor folder registers and links a vendor with it. The seed creates no referral codes - this one was created when Request Additional Role granted VENDOR.

item.description: Select any JPG, PNG or WEBP under 2 MB for the "file" field before sending - Postman cannot store a file inside a collection.

item.name: Delete Profile Image
item.description: Needs the image uploaded by the request above; without one it returns 400 NO_PROFILE_IMAGE.

item.name: Register Onboard - role not VENDOR/CUSTOMER (expect 400)
item.description: role must be VENDOR or CUSTOMER.

item.name: Sessions, Sign-out and Recovery
item.description: Runs last in the portal: it ends every session of this account.

item.name: Login BA (second device)
item.description: A second login creates a second session, so List Sessions has another device to revoke. The cookie jar now holds this newer session.

item.name: List Sessions (Devices)
item.description: Saves the sid of a session other than the current one into {{sid}}.

item.name: Login BA (again, for Logout)
item.description: Logout All Sessions ended every session; Logout below needs a live one.

item.name: Send Email Verification OTP
item.description: Always 200 with the same body. Only emails a code when the account exists and is not yet verified; every seeded account is already verified.

item.name: [manual] Verify Email
item.description: NEEDS A HUMAN: paste the code from the email into the {{otp}} collection variable before sending. Email is only delivered when EMAIL_USER / EMAIL_PASSWORD are set on the server; with them unset the code is never sent. Only an unverified account receives a code (a role with emailVerificationRequired=true; the development seed sets it false for every role).

item.name: [manual] Verify Reset OTP
item.description: NEEDS A HUMAN: paste the code from the email into the {{otp}} collection variable before sending. Email is only delivered when EMAIL_USER / EMAIL_PASSWORD are set on the server; with them unset the code is never sent. Uses the code emailed by Forgot Password. Sets the reset cookie that Reset Password needs.

item.name: [manual] Reset Password
item.description: Run straight after Verify Reset OTP: it needs the reset cookie that request sets. Resetting the password revokes every session of this account, so run this portal's Login again afterwards if you keep testing by hand.

item.name: [manual] Google Login
item.description: NEEDS A HUMAN: paste a real Google ID token into {{googleIdToken}}, and set GOOGLE_CLIENT_IDS on the server to the client id that minted it. With GOOGLE_CLIENT_IDS empty the provider is disabled and this returns 404 PROVIDER_NOT_AVAILABLE; with a bad token it returns 401.

item.name: Auth Scenarios
item.description: End-to-end auth behaviour, not endpoint coverage - the portal folders above already cover each route once. Run the numbered requests in order within each subfolder; they depend on the state the previous one leaves behind.

item.name: 0. Login as admin - the other-portal session request 11 lists
1. Login (customer, device A)

exec: pm.test('cookie is httpOnly and signed, carrying sid.secret', () => {

item.description: The session cookie value is s:<sid>.<secret>.<signature> (cookie-parser signing), URL-encoded. The response sets two cookies - the session and the CSRF one - so the test reads every Set-Cookie header rather than just one.

item.name: 2. Login again (device B)
item.description: A second login is a second device: the jar now holds device B's cookie, and device A's session is still alive for the next requests to find and revoke.

item.name: 3. List my devices
item.description: Saves the sid of the other device (device A) into {{otherSid}}.

item.name: 4. Revoke one device
item.description: Revokes device A using {{otherSid}}, saved by request 3.

item.name: 5. Revoke someone else's session - expect 404
item.description: Ownership check. A guessed sid must not be revocable.

item.name: [manual] 6. Google login
item.description: NEEDS A HUMAN: paste a real Google ID token into {{googleIdToken}}, and set GOOGLE_CLIENT_IDS on the server to the client id that minted it. With GOOGLE_CLIENT_IDS empty the provider is disabled and this returns 404 PROVIDER_NOT_AVAILABLE; with a bad token it returns 401.

item.name: 8. Rate limit - repeat to trip it
item.description: Login is limited per IP across all portals: RATE_LIMIT_LOGIN_MAX requests per RATE_LIMIT_LOGIN_WINDOW_SECONDS (code defaults 30 per 900 s). One send gets 401 for the wrong password. To see the limit, repeat just this request (Collection Runner, iterations) until a 429 with Retry-After. Each 401 also counts toward the lockout of customer@test.com (request 18).

exec: pm.test('401 for a wrong password', () => pm.response.to.have.status(401));
pm.test('session is dead after logout-all', () => pm.response.to.have.status(401));

item.name: 11. Admin - list devices
item.description: Same endpoint on another portal, with its own cookie: the admin session from request 0 is untouched by the customer logout-all above.

item.name: 12. Weak password rejected
item.description: Minimum length is PASSWORD_MIN_LENGTH (default 8), no composition rules. Enforced in password.service, not in the schema - one source of truth.

item.name: 13. Breached password rejected
item.description: HIBP k-anonymity check: only the first 5 SHA-1 chars leave the server. Fails OPEN, so a 201 here means HIBP was unreachable - not that the check is broken.

exec: pm.test('400 when HIBP knows it, 201 if HIBP unreachable (fails open)', () => {

item.name: 14. Invalid email rejected
item.description: zod at the edge. Before this, garbage fell through to the generic auth failure.

item.name: 15. OTP as a JSON number is accepted
item.description: Regression test. A numeric otp used to be compared against a stored string, always failing - and burning one of five attempts on a CORRECT code. A schema rejection would be 400 VALIDATION_ERROR; this must instead get past validation to the OTP check, which answers 400 AUTH_INVALID_OTP for this wrong code.

exec: pm.test('passes validation - the number is coerced, not rejected', () => pm.expect(pm.response.text()).to.not.include('VALIDATION_ERROR'));
pm.test('reaches the OTP check (400 AUTH_INVALID_OTP for a wrong or missing code)', () => {

item.name: 16. Login (customer) - a live session for the CSRF check
item.description: Logout all (request 9) ended every customer session. Without a live session, request 17 would be refused with 401 before CSRF is ever checked.

item.name: 17. Logout without CSRF header - expect 403
item.description: Deliberately sends NO x-csrf-token, so it must be refused even though the session from request 16 is valid.

item.name: 18. Lockout - repeat to lock the account
item.description: LOCKOUT_MAX_ATTEMPTS failures (default 5; this request and request 8 both count) inside LOCKOUT_WINDOW_SECONDS lock the account for LOCKOUT_DURATION_SECONDS. The response stays a GENERIC 401 even once locked - telling the caller "account locked" would confirm the address exists. The real reason is in the audit log. A successful login clears the failure count.

exec: pm.test('401 while under the cap, 401 generic once locked', () => {

item.name: 1. Forgot password - always 200
item.description: Returns the same body for a registered and an unregistered address. An OTP is stored either way - skipping the store for unknown addresses would make remainingAttempts null vs a number, which is an existence oracle by itself.

exec: pm.test('200 regardless of whether the address exists', () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));
pm.test('neutral message - no existence leak', () => pm.expect(pm.response.text()).to.match(/if that address/i));

item.name: 2. Forgot password - unknown address, identical response
item.description: Compare this response to request 1 byte for byte. Any difference is an enumeration hole.

exec: pm.test('200, same as a real address', () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));

item.name: 3. Wrong OTP burns an attempt
item.description: Runs against the code stored by request 1. Five wrong attempts per code (OTP_VERIFY_MAX_ATTEMPTS), then 429 AUTH_OTP_MAX_ATTEMPTS. Placed before the [manual] verify: a correct verify deletes the code, after which a wrong guess reports "expired" instead.

item.name: [manual] 4. Verify reset OTP - sets the reset cookie
item.description:
NEEDS A HUMAN: paste the code from the email into the {{otp}} collection variable before sending. Email is only delivered when EMAIL_USER / EMAIL_PASSWORD are set on the server; with them unset the code is never sent. Use the code from the email sent by request 1.

The reset id is 32 CSPRNG bytes.

exec: pm.test('200 with the correct code', () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));

item.name: [manual] 5. Reset password - weak one rejected
item.description:
Depends on [manual] request 4: without its reset cookie this is 401 AUTH_INVALID_RESET_SESSION, not the policy check.

The policy applies on reset, not only on register.

item.name: [manual] 6. Reset password - succeeds, kills every session
item.description:
Depends on [manual] request 4 (its reset cookie).

Also clears the account lockout - reset is the only recovery path a locked-out user has - and revokes every session. Verify by calling GET /sessions with an old cookie: it must 401.

item.name: 7. Reset session is single use
item.description: After [manual] request 6 the reset session is deleted, so replaying it must fail. When the manual requests were skipped there is no reset cookie at all, which must fail the same way.

exec: pm.test('401 - no usable reset session', () => pm.response.to.have.status(401));

item.name: 8. Send email verification code
item.description: Same enumeration-proof shape as forgot-password. Only actually emails when the account exists and is unverified.

exec: pm.test('does not reveal whether verification is needed', () => pm.expect(pm.response.text()).to.match(/if that address/i));

item.name: [manual] 9. Verify email
item.description:
NEEDS A HUMAN: paste the code from the email into the {{otp}} collection variable before sending. Email is only delivered when EMAIL_USER / EMAIL_PASSWORD are set on the server; with them unset the code is never sent. Use the code sent by request 8. customer@test.com is already verified, so no code is emailed to it; point requests 8 and 9 at an unverified account to exercise this.

Sets emailVerified and clears the OTP keys. Set {{otp}} from the code sent by request 7.

exec: pm.test('200 on the correct code', () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));

item.name: 10. Admin reset flow reaches the same handler
item.description: Spot check that a second portal routes into the same shared controller. Admin has no /register or /verify-email by design.

item.name: Session Cache Lifecycle
item.description: The session caches display fields, so every write that changes one must rewrite it (syncSessionUser) or destroy the session (revokeUserSessions). Run in order.

item.name: 2. /me serves the cached user - saves customerId

exec: pm.test('served from the session, not the database', () => pm.expect(u.email).to.eql('customer@test.com'));
// The whole point of syncSessionUser: no re-login needed.

item.name: 6. Admin suspends that customer
item.description: Uses {{customerId}}, saved by request 2.

exec: // Security-critical: authenticate no longer checks user.status, so revocation
// on suspend is the only thing ending a suspended account's access.
pm.test('401 - every session revoked on suspend', () => pm.response.to.have.status(401));

item.name: Role Scenarios
item.description: Admin role-request decisions, role toggles and portal-aware login, all checked against live sessions. Runs after Auth Scenarios; every role setting it changes is put back.

item.name: Role Requests
item.description: Admin approval of a self-service role request. Auto-approval is switched off for VENDOR and BUSINESS_ASSOCIATE first (and restored afterwards), so the requests stay PENDING whatever the environment - the development seed auto-approves both, production does not. Two admin-created accounts are used because admin-created users are approved and email-verified in every environment; creating them also gives each a referral code. A third account self-registers as BUSINESS_ASSOCIATE with the admin-created associate's referral code. Every approval runs the role-approved hook: the PENDING referral for that user and role becomes ACTIVE (the referrer's list and dashboard show it) and a BUSINESS_ASSOCIATE or VENDOR gets a referral code if it has none, so the approved associate can onboard users. An approval is also pushed into the requester's live sessions (sessionService.syncRoles), so the new role is switchable without logging in again. Run in order.

item.name: 15. Self-register a BUSINESS_ASSOCIATE with that referral code - PENDING
item.description: Auto-approve is off, so the account holds only a PENDING BUSINESS_ASSOCIATE role and no referral code, and its referral to the associate is PENDING. Registering sets no session cookie.

pm.test('lists the referral of rolereq.selfba@test.com', () => pm.expect(!!mine).to.be.true);

Role Toggle Live Sync
item.description: Deactivating a role is pushed into every live session of every holder: the role is removed from sessions acting as another role, and a session acting as the deactivated role is revoked. Uses the vendor from Role Requests, who now holds VENDOR and BUSINESS_ASSOCIATE. The last steps re-activate VENDOR so nothing after this folder is affected. Run in order.

item.name: 1. Vendor logs in to the associate portal too
item.description: Logs in the account from Role Requests, so the associate portal now has their session. The vendor-portal session from Role Requests is still live.

item.name: 4. Session acting as VENDOR is revoked - expect 401

exec: pm.test('401 Unauthorized - revoked, no re-login involved', () => pm.response.to.have.status(401));

item.name: 6. Associate session can no longer switch to VENDOR
7. Vendor portal login refused while VENDOR is inactive
Admin Portal Login as SUPER_ADMIN
item.description: The admin portal admits any role that maps to it, so an account holding SUPER_ADMIN but not ADMIN can log in there (pickPortalRole). The seed has no such account, so one is made through the API: SUPER_ADMIN is briefly made self-registrable, a fresh vendor requests it (SUPER_ADMIN auto-approves), and self-registration is closed again at once. The account is suspended at the end. Run in order; if a run stops part-way, make sure SUPER_ADMIN canSelfRegister is false again.
